prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: CC(C)(C)c1cc(NC(=O)Nc2ccc(-c3cn4c(n3)sc3cc(OCCN5CCOCC5)ccc34)cc2)no1
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL1974

Assay A:
  Description: Inhibition of wild type FLT3
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibition of human FLT3 using 10 uM ATP
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE" | "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
raw: {"call": "COMMENSURABLE", "confidence": 0.6, "error_class": "none", "reason": "Both assays measure IC50 inhibition of wild-type human FLT3 in biochemical binding/activity assays with high confidence scores; the specification of 10 uM ATP in Assay B is a standard kinase assay condition and unlikely to cause a large discrepancy unless Assay A used a very different ATP concentration, but both are likely comparable biochemical kinase inhibition assays."}

parsed.reason: Both assays measure IC50 inhibition of wild-type human FLT3 in biochemical binding/activity assays with high confidence scores; the specification of 10 uM ATP in Assay B is a standard kinase assay condition and unlikely to cause a large discrepancy unless Assay A used a very different ATP concentration, but both are likely comparable biochemical kinase inhibition assays.
